details: Bitcoin's price has demonstrated a heightened sensitivity to U.S. economic data releases, such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and employment reports, often showing stronger reactions than to actual Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. The upcoming CPI report on Friday, September 11, is widely anticipated to set the direction for Bitcoin, influencing market sentiment before the Federal Reserve's policy decision next week. A strong payrolls report on September 4 already contributed to pressure on Bitcoin's price.
title: US Economic Data Drives Bitcoin Volatility Ahead of CPI and Fed Decision

details: Bitcoin's value fell below $79,000 amid renewed expectations of a more restrictive monetary policy from the Federal Reserve. This sentiment was primarily driven by recent strong U.S. employment data, which could prompt the Fed to maintain or increase interest rates. Additionally, escalating oil prices and geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran are fueling inflation concerns, adding further pressure to cryptocurrency markets. Despite some support from institutional ETF inflows, short-term market momentum has weakened, and investor sentiment remains cautious ahead of upcoming U.S. inflation figures.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $79K as Fed Tightening Fears Intensify

details: The release of robust U.S. Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) data has led to a notable decline in confidence within the cryptocurrency market. This strong jobs report increases the probability of the Federal Reserve adopting a more aggressive monetary policy stance, making the financial environment less conducive for high-risk assets like cryptocurrencies. Consequently, this macroeconomic development has contributed to a period of market indecision, as investors assess the implications of potentially higher interest rates and reduced liquidity on digital assets.
title: Strong US Jobs Report Dents Crypto Market Confidence
